evals.name: apply-asset-package-failure
evals.prompt: Apply Asset Package keeps failing on our enterprise gdb when I try to add the gas domain to our existing water UN. Pro 3.5, Enterprise 11.3. What am I doing wrong?
evals.expected_output: Troubleshooting format; four prerequisites (maps closed, topology disabled, Pro/UN version match, owners + DEFAULT); notes additive behaviour.
assertions: Uses a troubleshooting structure (likely cause, checks in order, fix)
Mentions network topology must be disabled
Mentions closing all maps in the project
Mentions connecting as the database utility network owner and portal utility network owner
Mentions running while connected to the DEFAULT version
Explains that Apply Asset Package is additive so adding a domain network to an existing UN is supported

evals.name: rest-isolation-trace-json
evals.prompt: Write me the REST request to run an isolation trace from a water main (globalId {5B3C...}) at the midpoint, stopping at operable isolating valves, against version 'crew1.outage'. Domain network is Water, tier is Pressure.
evals.expected_output: Complete trace request with percentAlong 0.5, isolation traceType, filterBarriers using category Isolating + operable, gdbVersion; code output format.
assertions: traceType is isolation
starting point uses percentAlong (about 0.5), not terminalId, because it's a line
Sets gdbVersion to crew1.outage and does NOT require sessionId for a read-only trace (sessionId is only for a client holding the exclusive edit session)
Uses filterBarriers (or a category-based barrier) for isolating devices
domainNetworkName Water and tierName Pressure are in traceConfiguration
Operator values come from the valid set (e.g. equal) and values are strings

evals.name: dirty-area-status-decode
evals.prompt: our dirty areas table shows status values 1, 9 and 40 all over the place after a big load. which ones do I actually need to worry about?
evals.expected_output: Decodes 1 (edit only), 9 (edit + feature error), 40 (feature error + subnetwork error); says validate ignores error-only rows, so the feature must be edited; Update Subnetwork afterwards for bit 32.
assertions: Decodes 1 as a modified/inserted feature with no error
Decodes 9 as modified feature plus feature error
Decodes 40 as feature error plus subnetwork error
Says status 1 only needs validation while 9 and 40 need errors fixed
States that Validate Network Topology ignores error-only dirty areas (no edit bit) so the cause must be fixed by editing

evals.name: upgrade-v8-field-maps
evals.prompt: Should we upgrade our telecom + electric UN from version 7 to 8? We're on Enterprise 12.1 and Pro 3.7, and linemen use Field Maps.
evals.expected_output: Flags Field Maps/Native SDK don't support v8; lists upgrade prerequisites; weighs telecom benefits.
assertions: States Field Maps (and Native SDKs) do not support utility network version 8
Notes version 8 is mainly for the telecom domain network and is not the default
Lists Upgrade Dataset prerequisites (topology disabled, exclusive lock/services stopped, owner connections)
Recommends a backup before upgrading

evals.name: arcpy-structural-attachment
evals.prompt: python script to attach a transformer to a pole in our UN with arcpy — I have both globalids. also how would I remove it later
evals.expected_output: Uses arcpy.un.UtilityNetwork AddStructuralAttachmentAssociation and DeleteStructualAttachmentAssociation (Esri spelling); checks topology; licensing correct.
assertions: Uses arcpy.un.UtilityNetwork(...).AddStructuralAttachmentAssociation with structure and attachment tables and globalIds
Uses DeleteStructualAttachmentAssociation with Esri's spelling (or explicitly warns about it)
Mentions a structural attachment rule must exist for the asset types
Does not claim a separate 'Utility Network extension' license is required on current releases (Advanced Editing covers it from Enterprise 11.2)

evals.name: migrate-geometric-network-path
evals.prompt: we have an ArcMap geometric network for water and gas, 60k features, and want to move to the utility network in Pro. we like our own field names and don't want to adopt a full Foundation. what's the route and what do we need ready first?
evals.expected_output: Recommends the Migration Wizard or Migrate To Utility Network tool over a Foundation; names the service territory polygon prerequisite, geodatabase-class and Global ID requirements, and the analyze/resolve error loop.
assertions: Recommends the Migration Wizard or the Migrate To Utility Network geoprocessing tool for keeping the existing schema
Requires a service territory polygon covering current and future assets
States sources must be geodatabase classes (and that related classes or attachments need Global IDs)
Says the result is a basic UN needing error analysis (Analyze Network Data / Apply Error Resolutions) and later configuration
Does not claim the tool maps complex associations automatically

evals.name: foundation-schema-mapping
evals.prompt: we're loading our electric data into the Electric Foundation. how do we map our source subtypes to asset groups and asset types, and what do we do about our coded domain values that don't match?
evals.expected_output: Explains schema vs object mapping and the mapping workbook workflow: Create Simple Data Mapping, Create Migration Workspace, lookup tables, Load Data Using Workspace; notes database field names and expression-vs-lookup limits.
assertions: Describes the mapping Excel workbook produced by Create Simple Data Mapping (not the asset package tables) as where source-to-target mapping is defined
Mentions Create Migration Workspace and Load Data Using Workspace
Recommends lookup tables for mismatched domain values
Warns to use database field names rather than aliases
Warns a field cannot use both an expression and a lookup
Recommends disabling post-processing on the first deployment to review errors

evals.name: migration-relationship-classes
evals.prompt: our source geodatabase has a transformer-to-pole relationship class and some many-to-many relationship classes. what happens to them when we migrate to a UN?
evals.expected_output: Explains relationship classes map to associations (structural attachment for transformer-pole) via C_Associations and Sync the C Tables; many-to-many and attributed classes are not migrated by the Migrate To Utility Network tool.
assertions: Says transformer-to-pole maps to a structural attachment association
Mentions the C_Associations table and the Sync the C Tables tool (exclusive locks)
States many-to-many and attributed relationship classes cannot be migrated by the tool
Notes related classes need Global ID keys

evals.name: specific-apply-gas-to-water
evals.prompt: Apply Asset Package fails when I try to add gas to our water utility network. Setup: ArcGIS Pro 3.5, ArcGIS Enterprise 11.3 with PostgreSQL. Our water UN is 'WaterUN' in feature dataset 'WaterDistribution' and already has the domain network 'Water'. I'm applying the Gas Foundation asset package with 'Domain networks to apply' = Gas. My Pro project has two maps open (Editing and Publishing). I connected to the database as 'gis_editor' (the UN owner is 'wateradmin'), my Enterprise portal login is 'jsmith' (the portal utility network owner is 'wateradmin'), and my current version is 'wateradmin.crew1'. Network topology is currently enabled because dispatch runs traces all day. What exactly is wrong, in what order do I fix it, and will applying Gas wipe out our Water configuration?
evals.expected_output: Finds all five violated conditions, orders the fix, says the tool is additive, warns about dispatch downtime.
assertions: Names each violated condition: two open maps, topology enabled, database user not the owner, portal user not the portal owner, version not DEFAULT
Does not invent a Pro 3.5 / Enterprise 11.3 version mismatch (asks to check the dataset version instead)
Says Apply Asset Package is additive: Gas is added and Water is not removed or modified; select only Gas
Gives an ordered fix: backup and tell dispatch, close maps, portal owner sign-in and database owner connection on DEFAULT, disable topology, apply, then post-process/enable topology
Warns that disabling topology interrupts dispatch's traces

evals.name: specific-isolation-trace-crew1-outage
evals.prompt: Write the REST request for an isolation trace on our water utility network. Service: https://gis.cityutil.example/server/rest/services/WaterUN/UtilityNetworkServer (federated with our portal). The main is a WaterLine feature with GlobalID {8F2A6C1E-4B7D-4E1A-9C55-2D0F7A1B3E90}; break it at the midpoint. Isolating valves are in the WaterDevice class and carry the network category 'Isolating'; there is a network attribute 'Operable' where 1 means operable, and I only want to stop at operable valves. Domain network is Water, tier is Pressure. Run it on the branch version 'crew1.outage' (created by user crew1; someone else may have it open for editing). I also want to know which service connections lose water. Give me a curl command and tell me what to check if it comes back with zero elements.
evals.expected_output: Complete curl with percentAlong 0.5, filterBarriers (Isolating category and Operable), gdbVersion crew1.outage, no sessionId; explains element codes; zero-element checklist; validator output.
assertions: Start location uses percentAlong 0.5 and no terminalId
Uses filterBarriers (not conditionBarriers) with the Isolating category and Operable = "1" (string), joined with AND
gdbVersion is crew1.outage and sessionId is NOT required for a read-only trace; explains it is only for a client holding the exclusive edit session
States trace elements carry assetGroupCode/assetTypeCode and networkSourceId, not names, and identifies service connections via codes
Sets includeIsolated (or equivalent) so the affected features are returned
Zero-element checklist includes a silently ignored start location, the GlobalID not existing on that version, exact case-sensitive names, and dirty areas on the version
Runs scripts/build_trace_request.py --check and reports its real output

evals.name: specific-dirty-areas-8-and-40-survive-validate
evals.prompt: After loading 46k features into a branch version our DirtyAreas table has: Status 1 x 41,220; Status 2 x 130; Status 9 x 312; Status 8 x 5; Status 40 x 18. Validate Network Topology over the full extent says success, but the Status 8 and Status 40 rows are still there afterwards. What does each value mean, which ones do I actually need to work on, why did validate not clear them, and what do I do next for each?
evals.expected_output: Correct decode of 1, 2, 9, 8, 40; validate ignores error-only rows; edit the feature then validate; Update Subnetwork for 40.
assertions: Decodes 1 as insert/update, 2 as delete, 9 as insert/update plus feature error, 8 as feature error, 40 as feature error plus subnetwork error
Explains validate only evaluates dirty areas with an edit bit, so error-only rows 8 and 40 are ignored (not a failed validate)
Says the fix for 8 and 40 is to edit the feature, rule or subnetwork definition, then validate
Says 40 also needs Update Subnetwork and that the subnetwork stays Invalid until it updates cleanly
Says 9 rows are re-evaluated and become 8 if the error persists
Says a successful validate job does not mean zero errors

evals.name: pro-sdk-validate-no-job
evals.prompt: Pro add-in C#: I want to validate topology for the current map extent and know if the network still has dirty areas. Do I use Job<T> and HasValidNetworkTopology?
evals.expected_output: Uses ValidateNetworkTopology returning ValidationResult on the MCT; GetState for dirty areas; no Job<T>.
assertions: Uses utilityNetwork.ValidateNetworkTopology(...) wrapped in QueuedTask.Run, returning a ValidationResult
Says Job<T> / UtilityNetworkValidationJob is not part of the Pro SDK UtilityNetwork API (it belongs to the Maps SDK for .NET)
Uses GetState() (UtilityNetworkState: HasDirtyAreas, IsNetworkTopologyEnabled) instead of HasValidNetworkTopology, which is arcpy-only
Notes ValidateNetworkTopology cannot run inside an edit operation (use ValidateNetworkTopologyInEditOperation in an add-in)

evals.name: rest-validate-discovered
evals.prompt: After calling validateNetworkTopology async from REST, which property lists the subnetworks it found, and what is in each item?
evals.expected_output: discoveredSubnetworks with domain, tier, subnetwork per item.
assertions: Names the property discoveredSubnetworks (not 'discovered')
Says each entry has domain, tier and subnetwork
Notes returnEdits is ignored when async=true

evals.name: js-add-association-name
evals.prompt: In the JS SDK, how do I add a connectivity association between two junctions and save it?
evals.expected_output: Uses generateAddAssociations (plural, array) then applyEdits.
assertions: Uses utilityNetwork.generateAddAssociations with an array of Association objects (plural), not generateAddAssociation
Applies the returned ServiceEdits via applyEdits on the associations table or feature service
Does not recommend the deprecated UtilityNetworkTrace widget classes for new 5.x apps

evals.name: telecom-circuit-rest
evals.prompt: From REST, how do I create a telecom circuit and then list the circuits that consume it? What release is needed?
evals.expected_output: Circuits and unit identifiers arrived at Enterprise 12.1; create takes startLocation/stopLocation; query uses circuitHierarchy.
assertions: States circuits and unit identifiers need Enterprise 12.1 (not 11.5)
Uses startLocation/stopLocation with firstUnit/lastUnit, not startPoint/numUnits
Uses circuitHierarchy (consumers/providers) to find consuming circuits; does not invent returnConsumingCircuits

evals.name: path-vs-shortest-path
evals.prompt: Which trace should I use to find two alternative routes between two points in a fiber and a water network?
evals.expected_output: Path trace (12.1+) with Num Paths; shortest path deprecated; Infer Connectivity telecom-only.
assertions: Says Shortest path is deprecated at Pro 3.7 / Enterprise 12.1 and Path replaces it
Notes Num Paths applies to Path and needs Enterprise 12.1+
Notes stopping points are required for traditional networks but optional for telecom, and Infer Connectivity is telecom-only

evals.name: apportionable-attribute
evals.prompt: Can I make a Short network attribute apportionable so it splits across a partially traced line?
evals.expected_output: No: apportionable is Double only, and only for line features.
assertions: States only Double attributes can be apportionable
Notes apportionment is meant for line features across edge elements

evals.name: owner-rights-enable-topology
evals.prompt: Who has to connect to run Enable Network Topology on an enterprise UN, and does Update Subnetwork need the owner?
evals.expected_output: Both the database owner connection and the portal owner; Update Subnetwork needs neither owner.
assertions: Says Enable Network Topology needs both the database owner connection and the portal owner sign-in
Says Update Subnetwork and Validate do not need an owner connection
Does not claim a separate Utility Network extension is needed on current releases (Advanced Editing)

evals.name: dirty-area-error-ids
evals.prompt: Error Inspector shows error ID 43 on a feature and we also see 41 on a subnetwork. Which bit is that in Status, and is it the same kind of error?
evals.expected_output: Esri does not map error IDs to Status bits; 43 is enable/validate, 41 is update-subnetwork.
assertions: Does not claim a fixed mapping from error ID to Status bit
Identifies 43 as an enable/validate topology error and 41 as an update-subnetwork error per Esri's tables
Suggests checking the Dirty Areas attribute table for the Status and error code

evals.name: export-subnetwork-ack
evals.prompt: What does exportAcknowledgement do in exportSubnetwork, and can I run it on a named version?
evals.expected_output: Requires DEFAULT; if all controllers are logically deleted, exporting removes the Subnetworks rows and produces no file.
assertions: Says exportAcknowledgement requires the DEFAULT version
Explains exporting a subnetwork whose controllers are all logically deleted physically deletes its row and creates no JSON file

evals.name: explain-ut-from-scratch
evals.prompt: I'm new to the utility network. Explain how it actually works - what happens from the moment someone edits a device to the moment a trace is right?
evals.expected_output: Teaches the stored vs computed model and the edit lifecycle (edit, dirty area, validate, subnetwork update, trace).
assertions: Explains that connectivity is stored as logical connectivity/associations and the network topology is a computed index built by Validate
Describes dirty areas created by edits and cleared by Validate Network Topology
Says subnetworks are updated separately (Update Subnetwork) and that trace results depend on the topology being validated
Distinguishes edits from error-only dirty areas (Status 8/16/32) which Validate ignores

evals.name: rules-default-deny
evals.prompt: Editors can't connect a new device to a line: 'no rule exists'. Do we just need to import more rules, and what exactly does the engine check?
evals.expected_output: Explains default-deny rule model, rule keying and how to fix.
assertions: Explains the UN is default-deny: a connection or containment without a matching rule is rejected
Explains rules are keyed by asset group/type (and terminals where relevant) and checked at edit/validate time
Suggests checking the asset type is correct before adding rules, and using Add Rule / Import Rules

evals.name: network-attribute-bits
evals.prompt: We want 40 new in-line network attributes for a water network. Any limit we should know about?
evals.expected_output: In-line attribute bit budget, nothing invented.
assertions: Explains In Line network attributes share a bit budget and states the figure only as Esri documents it (25 bits user-defined of 64)
Notes that attribute size (bits) depends on the domain/data type and sequential coded values from 0
Does not invent a count limit that Esri does not state

evals.name: partitioned-vs-hierarchical
evals.prompt: How do we choose between a partitioned and a hierarchical domain network, and can we change it later?
evals.expected_output: Explains the choice and its permanence.
assertions: Explains partitioned tiers (disjoint, a feature belongs to one) versus hierarchical (a feature may belong to several levels)
States the choice is made when the domain network is added and cannot be changed later (or says to verify)
Mentions tier ranks and subnetwork controllers

evals.name: trace-too-wide
evals.prompt: My upstream trace returns the whole network. Why and what do I tune?
evals.expected_output: Trace diagnosis via traversability, barriers, flow direction.
assertions: Checks flow direction (controllers, digitized direction, indeterminate flow) and starting point terminal
Mentions condition barriers, filter barriers and traversability scope
Mentions that containers/structures or output filters change what comes back

evals.name: pro-build-order
evals.prompt: What's the order of geoprocessing steps to build a utility network by hand in Pro, and who has to be connected as the owner for each?
evals.expected_output: Ordered build flow with owner connection per step.
assertions: Gives the order: create utility network, add domain network(s), add tiers, rules/terminal configurations/network attributes/categories, enable network topology, load data, validate, controllers, update subnetwork
States that enable/disable topology need both the database owner connection and the portal owner, while Validate and Update Subnetwork need neither
Notes dataset version must be chosen explicitly (v8) at Pro 3.7 / Enterprise 12.1

evals.name: which-api-for-addin
evals.prompt: We need to automate nightly validate and update subnetwork on Enterprise and also build a Pro add-in. Which API for each?
evals.expected_output: API decision per surface.
assertions: Recommends arcpy.un (GP tools) or REST for unattended nightly jobs and the Pro SDK for the add-in
Does not offer the ArcGIS API for Python for utility network operations
Mentions Pro SDK calls run on the MCT via QueuedTask

evals.name: versions-two-editors
evals.prompt: Two editors worked in named versions and both posted. What do we need to redo on DEFAULT before the data is trustworthy?
evals.expected_output: Post-reconcile steps.
assertions: Says to validate network topology on DEFAULT and then update subnetworks, because named-version work may not be authoritative
Notes the reconcile exclusive lock and sessionId behaviour at the Enterprise version in use or says to verify
Mentions checking errors/dirty areas after the post

evals.name: status-bits-learning
evals.prompt: What's the difference between Status, error code and error ID in the dirty areas table?
evals.expected_output: Disambiguates three similar concepts.
assertions: Explains Status is a bitmask (1/2/4 edit, 8/16/32 error), error code is a separate field, and error ID is Esri's catalogue number
States Esri does not map error IDs to Status bits
Says to read the Dirty Areas attribute table for Status and error code
